case.question: I fish from the pier for salmon. For this week, how good do you expect pier fishing for salmon to be at each of St. Joseph, South Haven, Grand Haven and Muskegon? Rate each port 0-4 (0 slow, 1 below average, 2 average, 3 good, 4 excellent) and say which you'd go to.

events.text:
## Recommendation

- **Go to the Grand Haven pier.** It is my pick, though it is a weak pick: I'd rate it 2 of 4 (average).
- Muskegon: 1 of 4. St. Joseph and South Haven: about 1 of 4, with low confidence because neither has a recent pier report.
- Fish early and low-light, when the pier bite has been best. Start with glow spoons or glow plugs and white flies, or live alewife or gizzard shad if you can get them.
- Expect slow fishing. Pier anglers have reported slow or no salmon for most of the last month, so treat any catch as a bonus.

## Why

- Grand Haven's pier was the only one in the last four weeks rated good, with salmon taken from the pierheads in 70 feet of water on glow spoons, glow plugs, white flies and live bait (Grand Haven, 2026-08-26).
- I'd expect Grand Haven to do better than Muskegon because its pier reports have been slightly better and its recent cooling is more consistent with a pier bite. Muskegon's last two pier reports were both slow (Muskegon, 2026-09-09 and 2026-09-02).
- St. Joseph and South Haven get a higher score for cooling water, but I found no pier reports from either port in the last four weeks, so I can't confirm a pier bite there.
- I'd expect the pier bite to be slow overall. In past seasons, pier anglers in similar water near 62 F mostly reported slow fishing (Muskegon, 2024-10-09; South Haven, 2024-10-09; Grand Haven, 2023-09-06).

## Evidence

**Recent reports (latest 2026-09-09, 13 days old)**
- Grand Haven, 2026-09-09: pier rated 0 (slow). Anglers casting spoons reported no salmon. Boats did better, rated 3 (good), 65–100 ft down in 85–140 ft of water, on green and white flies.
- Muskegon, 2026-09-09: pier rated 0. "Pier anglers were unsuccessful targeting salmon due to warm water temperatures." Boats rated 2 (average).
- South Haven, 2026-09-09 and St. Joseph, 2026-09-09: no pier data. Boats rated 1 and 2.
- Grand Haven, 2026-09-02 and Muskegon, 2026-09-02: pier both rated 0, "due to increased/warmer water conditions."
- Grand Haven, 2026-08-26: the one good pier result (rated 3), with the report noting a sharp water drop that week.

**Past seasons (similar surface temperature, about 62 F ±4)**
- Pier results were mostly 0 or 1. Examples: Grand Haven, 2023-09-06 (0, "slow", glow spoons); Grand Haven, 2023-09-20 (1, a few salmon on glow spoons early in the morning); Grand Haven, 2024-10-02 (0, slow); St. Joseph, 2022-10-05 (0, slow).
- Grand Haven, 2024-09-11: pier anglers caught coho and Chinook on alewives and glow spoons (not rated).

**Conditions (week before 2026-09-22; see caveat on the live feed)**
- Buoy surface water averaged 59–65 F that week, down 10–17 F over the week at all four ports.
- Satellite water near the pier dropped about 9 F in the last 3 days at St. Joseph and South Haven, and about 2 F at Grand Haven and Muskegon.
- Upwelling-favorable wind (north to east, 8+ mph) totaled 33 hours in the last 3 days at St. Joseph, 44 at South Haven, 47 at Grand Haven and 52 at Muskegon.

## Caveats

- The newest pier report is from 2026-09-09, 13 days old. Ratings are estimates from older reports, not current conditions.
- The conditions tool was in backtest mode ("live data is unavailable") and returned a summary of the past week, not a live reading. It did not include pierhead water temperature or a wind forecast for this weekend, so check the forecast before you go.
- The satellite water values come from GLSEA, which can lag by 1–2 days. The buoy averages are miles offshore.
- St. Joseph and South Haven have no pier reports in the last four weeks, so those ratings rest on the conditions and past seasons only.
